supported_range: Agent Zero v1.14+ and the whole V2 line
note: Baseline for tools/a0_upgrade_check.py. `fingerprints` are whitespace- and comment-insensitive hashes of each watched symbol's source in the verified Agent Zero tag. Re-pin ONLY through `--update-baseline`, and only after a clean audit. v1.0.9 shrank this list: KAME now delegates the model call to Agent Zero instead of re-implementing it, so the stream parser, the chunk accumulator, the transport parser, the result builder and litellm itself left KAME's compatibility surface entirely. Agent Zero's OAuth / subscription providers (Codex, Copilot, ...) are deliberately NOT in this list: KAME reads keys from the .env directly and never goes through models.get_api_key, which is where the OAuth plugin hooks in, so there is no shared symbol to fingerprint. That independence is guarded behaviorally instead, by the LIVE 3 block in tests/test_a0_compat.py.

severity_legend.critical: if this breaks, KAME does not rotate at all
severity_legend.degraded: if this breaks, ONE shield stops; rotation keeps working
severity_legend.adaptive: KAME handles a change here automatically - the fingerprint is informational
severity_legend.optional: the symbol only exists from some A0 version onward - MISSING is expected on older builds and never fails the check

watch.why: KAME wraps this and calls it back. Since v1.0.9 it is found BY SHAPE (a coroutine taking messages + response/reasoning/tokens callbacks), so a RENAME is survivable and the body may change freely - KAME never parses what it returns. What still matters: it must keep accepting `api_key` through **kwargs, and keep at least those four parameter names.

Same contract as unified_call (A0 V2.1+ routes the monologue here). Its return value is passed straight back to A0's caller, so its type may change freely; KAME only reads .response / .reasoning to detect a fully empty answer, and tolerates their absence.
_get_all_api_keys reads API_KEY_<PROVIDER> / <PROVIDER>_API_KEY / <PROVIDER>_API_TOKEN through it. No keys found = no rotation at all, on every provider.

KAME ships an activation extension at the @extensible-derived path _functions/agent/Agent/monologue/start. Since v1.0.9 this is no longer the only door: activation also ships at the NAMED points agent_init and monologue_start, so losing this path costs nothing as long as agent.py still calls those.

_kame_honor_intervention() calls it between rotations and during cooling sleeps so a user nudge is never slept through. If it moves, a nudge during a long outage waits for the next A0-side callback instead.

KAME Shield's tool-arg healer ships at _functions/agent/Agent/validate_tool_request/start. Derived-path fragility: if it moves, the healer stops firing and a malformed tool call is no longer salvaged.
The arg shape KAME Shield heals into. Which keys it reads (text / message) decides whether the salvage still lands.

KAME monkey-patches this for the compression timeout guard (it tags compression calls so the carousel can prefer fresh keys). Wrapped in its own try since v1.0.9 - a failure here can no longer stop rotation from installing.
Same as Topic.summarize_messages, for bulk compression.
KAME swaps its asyncio.Lock for a threading.Lock and replaces cleanup/get_total. Depends on ._lock, .values and .timeframe. Isolated since v1.0.9.
In KAME's passthrough tuple - it must reach A0's repair loop, never be swallowed as a failed API call. If the import fails KAME degrades to an empty passthrough tuple rather than crashing.

Added in A0 v2.4: aborts a turn after N consecutive UNPARSEABLE model outputs. KAME's _95_kame_unusable_floor raises that limit to a floor, and to do so it reads A0's own counter out of loop_data.params_persistent['_unusable_response_failures'] and only ever clears a HandledException. If A0 renames that state key or stops staging the abort in data['exception'], the floor silently stops lifting and A0's own limit applies again - rotation is untouched. Absent on A0 < v2.4, where the shield is inert by design (marked optional: a MISSING here is expected, not a break).
